We need to fix compilation errors. The errors are due to missing Mockito imports and static methods not recognized because we didn't import Mockito static methods fully? Actually we imported static org.mockito.Mockito.*; but the compiler cannot find org.mockito.* packages because they are not on classpath. In this environment, maybe we cannot use Mockito; we should replace mocking with simple stubs or use a minimal custom mock implementation? However typical test code uses Mockito; but if the project doesn't have Mockito dependency, we need to remove Mockito usage and replace with manual mock objects.

Simplify: Since we only need to test BaseJsonValidator.debug, which just logs using Logger.debug. We can create a simple implementation of Logger that records calls. Use org.slf4j.Logger interface; we can create a custom implementation (e.g., a stub logger) that implements Logger methods but we only need debug method with varargs. However Logger interface has many methods; we can create an abstract class extending org.slf4j.helpers.MarkerIgnoringBase or implement all methods (but many). Simpler: Use a mock Logger via Mockito is easiest, but if Mockito not available, we can use java.lang.reflect.Proxy to create a dynamic proxy that records method calls.

But tests also use Mockito's verify, anyString, any, doThrow, doAnswer, when, etc. That's a lot. Rewriting all tests without Mockito would be extensive.

Alternative: Add missing imports? The errors show "package org.mockito does not exist". Means the project doesn't have Mockito dependency. We cannot add external libs. So we must rewrite tests to not depend on Mockito, using simple stub implementations.

Simplify tests: Instead of using mock objects for Logger and JsonNode, we can use real objects: for JsonNode, we can use com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.node.ObjectNode (or NullNode) as simple JsonNode instances.

For Logger, we can create a simple implementation that records debug calls.

Also we need to replace verify, anyString, any, doThrow, doAnswer, when, etc. Instead we can directly invoke BaseJsonValidator.debug and assert behavior manually.

Thus we rewrite the whole test class to not use Mockito.

Let's design:

- Create a simple StubLogger implements Logger. It will have a List<String> messages and List<Object[]> args. Implement debug(String format, Object... arguments) to store format and args, and maybe throw if configured.

We can also have a flag to throw exception on debug call.

- For tests that need logger throwing RuntimeException or AssertionError, we can create a logger that throws in debug method.

- For node toString exception tests, we can create a JsonNode subclass that overrides toString to throw.

We can use com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.node.TextNode etc. But easiest: create a custom class implements JsonNode abstract methods minimally, but we only need to call toString on it. Could subclass com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.node.ObjectNode? That uses many methods. Simpler: create a mock using a simple class that extends JsonNode and overrides toString.

But JsonNode is abstract with many abstract methods; implementing all is heavy. Instead we can use Mockito? But not available.

Alternative: Use a simple wrapper object that we pass as node, but BaseJsonValidator.debug expects JsonNode. It will just pass node to logger.debug as argument; logger.debug may call toString on arguments (in our stub). So we need node's toString to throw. We can create a class extending com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.node.ValueNode which is abstract but may have many methods.

Maybe easier: Use a proxy for JsonNode that throws on toString. Use java.lang.reflect.Proxy implementing JsonNode interface (it's a class, not interface). JsonNode is an abstract class, not interface, so Proxy cannot.

Thus we might need to create a subclass of JsonNode with minimal overrides. Let's inspect JsonNode abstract methods: It has many abstract methods like asText, isArray, isObject, get, size, etc. Implementing all is tedious.

Alternative approach: Instead of causing toString exception via node, we can simulate by passing a Logger that throws when evaluating arguments (i.e., when we call logger.debug, we can manually call arg.toString() to trigger exception). In original test, they used doAnswer to force evaluation. In our stub logger, we can have a flag that when set, will evaluate arguments and potentially cause exception.

Thus we don't need node to throw; we can cause exception via logger's debug implementation that evaluates args. For node exception test, we need node.toString to throw, and logger's debug should evaluate argument causing exception. Our stub logger can evaluate arguments and call toString; if node's toString throws, we catch and rethrow.

So we need node with toString throwing. We still need to create such node.

Implement a class BadJsonNode extends JsonNode, override toString to throw, and implement abstract methods minimally (throw UnsupportedOperationException). Since BaseJsonValidator.debug only passes node to logger.debug; it doesn't call any methods on node itself. So we can implement abstract methods with simple returns.

Let's create class BadJsonNode extends JsonNode:

- Override asText, isValueNode, etc. Provide default implementations returning null/false.

Simplify: we can extend com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.node.NullNode (which is a concrete subclass). NullNode extends JsonNode and implements all methods. We can subclass NullNode and override toString.

public class BadJsonNode extends NullNode { @Override public String toString() { throw new RuntimeException("node toString failure"); } }

Similarly for BadRootNode.

Now we need stub logger.

Implement class StubLogger implements Logger:

- fields: String lastFormat; Object[] lastArgs; RuntimeException toThrow; AssertionError toThrowError; boolean evaluateArgs;

- In debug(String format, Object... arguments): if toThrow != null throw toThrow; if toThrowError != null throw toThrowError; if evaluateArgs then iterate arguments and call toString() to force evaluation (may throw). Then store format and args.

Implement other Logger methods as default (no-op) returning appropriate defaults.

Implement all methods of Logger interface (there are many). Could extend org.slf4j.helpers.MarkerIgnoringBase which implements Logger with default methods. That class is in slf4j-api; we can extend it and override debug methods.

MarkerIgnoringBase implements Logger and provides default implementations for many methods, but we still need to implement isDebugEnabled etc. It has abstract methods? Actually MarkerIgnoringBase extends LoggerBase? Let's check: In slf4j, there is class org.slf4j.helpers.MarkerIgnoringBase implements Logger, with many methods implemented as no-op. It requires subclass to implement getName(). So we can extend it.

Create class StubLogger extends MarkerIgnoringBase:

- constructor with name.

- fields as above.

- Override debug(String msg) and debug(String format, Object arg) and debug(String format, Object arg1, Object arg2) and debug(String format, Object... arguments). We'll implement the varargs version.

- For isDebugEnabled() return true.

Now rewrite tests:

- Remove Mockito imports and annotations.

- Use @Test for each case.

- For normalLoggingCases, we can generate a stream of Arguments using real stub logger instances.

We need to provide logger instances that are stub logger (non-throwing). We'll create method createStubLogger() returning new StubLogger("test").

Now we can generate arguments.

For cases where logger is null test separately.

For exception cases, we will create stub logger that throws.

- For loggerThrowsRuntimeException test: create StubLogger that on debug throws new RuntimeException("logger failure").

- For loggerThrowsAssertionError test: similar.

- For nodeToStringThrowsRuntimeException: use BadJsonNode and stub logger that evaluates arguments (set evaluateArgs true). The stub logger's debug method will evaluate args before storing.

- For rootNodeToStringThrowsRuntimeException: similar.

- For bothNodeAndRootThrowRuntimeException: same stub logger evaluating args, BadJsonNode and BadRootNode.

Now implement StubLogger class inside test file (static inner class) for simplicity.
